🚨 THE SOURCE HAD A CONTROLLED-SUBSTANCE TYPO ON THE LABEL, AND IT WAS REPAIRED RATHER THAN PUBLISHED AS-IS. The frame Malcolm chose reads '2% GHB-CU'. The ingredient is GHK-Cu (glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine copper); GHB is gamma-hydroxybutyrate, a controlled substance. Confirmed at native 3072px before claiming it, not at display size. Publishing it unaltered was not an option, and he asked for it fixed rather than swapped.

THE FAULT TRACKS RESOLUTION, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE FINDING. Every 2048px frame in this wave is correct; both 3072px frames are wrong:
  run-01/1,2,3 (2048) GHK-CU ok   |   run-01/4 (3072) GHB-CU BAD
  run-02/1,2,3 (2048) GHK-CU ok   |   run-02/4 (3072) GHB-CU BAD
So a higher-resolution sibling is a DIFFERENT photograph needing its own label read, never a better copy of the same one. This is also the third spelling of this ingredient seen on artwork: GHK-CU (right), GHD-CU, and now GHB-CU — check the letter, do not pattern-match the shape.

HOW THE GLYPH WAS REPAIRED. Only the B was touched; every other pixel of the photograph is untouched. Measured first: cap height 46px (rows 2166-2211), stroke width 7px, B box x1213-1244, taken from column/row profiles rather than by eye.
  1. Ground rebuilt across x1213-1244 by per-row linear interpolation between two columns that are provably background — x1208-1212 (clear: G ends 1171, H is 1177-1207) and x1245-1248 (clear: the hyphen starts at 1249). Grain re-added from x1018-1049, the only window between the '|' at 1010-1017 and the '2' at 1051.
  2. The B's own left stem (x1213-1221) pasted back untouched, so the K's vertical is literally the original pixels — identical weight, colour, emboss and noise.
  3. The two arms drawn at 6x supersample and downsampled, in the glyph colour sampled from the H's stem core, with the label's own drop-shadow colour offset down-right to match the emboss.

TWO OF MY OWN BUGS ARE WORTH RECORDING, because both produced a plausible-looking artefact rather than an obvious failure. Sampling the right-hand interpolation anchor at x1250-1256 pulled in the WHITE HYPHEN and painted a bright vertical stripe through the ground. Sampling the grain patch at x1350+ pulled in the '|' SEPARATOR and painted a pale rectangular block. In both cases the arithmetic was fine and the source window was wrong — when an inpaint shows a clean-edged artefact, suspect the sample window before the algorithm.

VERIFIED AT THREE SCALES, because a label can survive one and fail another: at 8x (letterform and emboss read native), at 1:1 (reads GHK-CU), and at the 660px render size this block actually serves (still reads GHK-CU). Seam checked numerically too — max adjacent-column jump on pure-background rows is 5.67, inside the natural grain, so no visible edge. The resize to 3000px and the q95 encode were done BEFORE the final check, so what was verified is exactly what ships.

RESOLUTION: 3072 capped to 3000, the widest the theme's srcset ever requests, done here rather than left to the uploader so the verified file is the uploaded file. The outgoing file is 1024x1024, so this is an upgrade.
